title: Group: legal entity register and organization charts
source_system: Corporate secretary's entity management system; HR organization charts
what_it_shows: A holding company (SEC registrant) with three operating subsidiaries: Specialty Chemicals, Chemical Distribution and Hazmat Transport. Corporate shared services (identity, network, security operations, OT security engineering, cloud and data platform, ERP, the Group Emergency Response Center, the process safety center of excellence, HR, finance, legal and internal audit) sit in the parent. Organization charts show the Group CISO, the Group OT Security Director reporting to the Group CISO, the Group Process Safety Director, the Group Chief Risk Officer, three division security and compliance leads, and plant security coordinators at the 7 formerly tiered plants

title: Group: HR roster by division
source_system: Group HR and payroll system (SYS-G4)
what_it_shows: 45,000 employees: Specialty Chemicals about 24,000 (Plant C1 about 1,150), Distribution about 9,500 (Terminal T1 about 140), Hazmat Transport about 6,000 (about 2,700 drivers), corporate shared services about 5,500. Driver home addresses include Illinois and Colorado, and about 110 drivers live in California. Termination events feed SYS-G1 identity governance

title: Group: FY2025 revenue by division
source_system: ERP general ledger (SYS-G4); FY2025 Form 10-K segment note
what_it_shows: Revenue of about $18.0 billion: Specialty Chemicals about $11.4 billion, Distribution about $5.6 billion from third parties, Hazmat Transport about $1.0 billion from third parties, plus about $0.7 billion of intercompany revenue eliminated in consolidation

title: Group: FY2025 Form 10-K cybersecurity disclosure and disclosure committee charter
source_system: SEC filings; disclosure committee records
what_it_shows: The FY2025 annual report includes the Regulation S-K Item 106 disclosure (risk management, board risk committee oversight and the Group CISO's reporting line). The disclosure committee charter covers cybersecurity incidents; its materiality factors do not mention OT or process safety consequences such as a release, a plant outage or utility supply

title: Group: ERM risk acceptance standard and 2025 risk registers
source_system: GRC tool (enterprise risk module)
what_it_shows: Risk acceptance authority: Very Low and Low by the division security and compliance lead, Moderate by the division president, High by the Group Chief Risk Officer with the Group CISO (reported to the board risk committee), Very High by the board risk committee only. Process safety and public safety risks rated High must be treated, not accepted. The 2025 group and division registers are on file

title: Group: board risk committee and audit committee minutes, 2025 to 2026-Q1
source_system: Board portal
what_it_shows: The board risk committee oversees group cyber and process safety risk and receives the High risk list each quarter; group internal audit reports to the board audit committee

title: Group: internal audit charter, 2026 audit plan and prior assessment records
source_system: Group internal audit records
what_it_shows: Internal audit reports to the board audit committee and neither designs nor operates controls. Common controls are assessed once a year with division samples. The Hazmat Transport assessment records for 2024 and 2025 cover the carrier's own procedures; they list no group controls the division inherits and no tests of dispatch, telematics or ELD measures

title: Group: policy library (group policies, 2025 edition) and group standards
source_system: Group policy repository
what_it_shows: Group policies POL-01 to POL-05 (2025 edition) aligned to NIST CSF 2.0. Group standards and plans on file: logging (security logs kept 1 year online and 6 years archived), passwords (minimum length 14 with banned-password checks), cryptography and key management, physical security, personnel security, acquisition, system integrity, and the supply chain risk management plan (2025). The library has no AI standard

title: Group: OT security standard (2025), architecture annex and deployment tracker
source_system: Group policy repository; OT security program records
what_it_shows: The 2025 OT security standard sets the OT DMZ pattern, zones and conduits, remote access only through the group gateway, passive OT monitoring, hardening checklists, a rule that mobile devices may not connect to OT networks (section 5), security review in OT projects (design review of the 2025 OT DMZ project on file), and an OT procurement template with security requirements. The tracker shows the standard deployed at 9 of 16 plants (including Plant C1) and at Terminal T1; the 7 legacy plants are scheduled to migrate by 2027-12-31

title: Group: division policy supplements and policy register
source_system: Group policy repository
what_it_shows: The Specialty Chemicals and Distribution supplements are recorded as aligned to the 2025 group policies. The Hazmat Transport supplement v2023 was last aligned 2023-04 and has no review date after its owner changed. It allows shared ELD support and terminal front-office accounts, requires MFA for email only, sets account removal by the end of the next business day, uses its own 3-level incident severity scale, limits the security plan to physical threats, and does not address AI use or common control inheritance

title: Group: common control catalog and inheritance matrices
source_system: Group GRC tool
what_it_shows: The catalog lists 116 common controls provided by SYS-G1 to SYS-G3 and group functions. Inheritance matrices exist for Specialty Chemicals (2025) and Distribution (2026); none was provided for Hazmat Transport

title: Group: SYS-G1 authentication and sign-in policy export
source_system: Group identity platform admin console (SYS-G1)
what_it_shows: 45,000 unique workforce identities assigned from HR records and never reused. MFA with number matching for all workforce sign-ins to SSO applications; phishing-resistant authenticators for IT administrators and central engineers; replay-resistant protocols; lockout after 10 failed attempts with risk-based sign-in blocking; re-authentication when a session is elevated; validated cryptographic modules per the vendor documentation

title: Group: SYS-G1 identity governance export and access request procedures
source_system: Identity governance module (SYS-G1)
what_it_shows: Joiner-mover-leaver workflows driven by HR events for all three divisions; corporate accounts disabled within 4 hours of termination; transfers trigger an access review within 5 business days; accounts of individuals posing significant risk disabled within 1 hour on HR or security request; access requests approved in workflow; Q1 2026 certification of IT applications completed. Plant OT domains have no trust to the corporate directory and are not in the workflows

title: Group: privileged access management inventory, policy and vault report
source_system: Privileged access management console (SYS-G1)
what_it_shows: Just-in-time elevation with session recording for IT administrators; OT domain administrator credentials at plants on the OT standard are vaulted and checked out through PAM; administrators and engineers use separate non-privileged accounts for email and office work, and OT administrator accounts have no mailbox

title: Group: OT remote access gateway configuration, account list and policies (SYS-G1)
source_system: OT remote access gateway admin console; gateway policy export; session recording settings
what_it_shows: The gateway serves 17 sites (16 plants and Terminal T1) for 14 integrators and OEMs and the central engineering hub (SYS-C8), with MFA. Integrator access uses team accounts, each shared by the team's members with one MFA device; no site approval step is configured before a session connects; session recording is enabled at 9 of the 17 sites (Plant C1 and Terminal T1 included); the hub holds standing connections to the engineering workstations at all 16 plants. Sessions end after 8 hours or 30 minutes idle; client split tunneling is blocked; sessions are encrypted end to end to the site jump hosts; broker hosts on provider A are patched monthly

title: Group: SIEM data sources, detection rules, OT desk use cases and sensor coverage map
source_system: Group SIEM and OT monitoring console (SYS-G2)
what_it_shows: 24x7 SOC with an OT desk since 2025. Data sources include SYS-G1, the gateway, firewalls, cloud accounts, EDR, the Terminal T1 OT and IT logs and the plant OT domains; account use cases UC-ID-01 to UC-ID-06; OT rules alert on new devices, firmware downloads and engineering commands outside approved windows; log source failures alert within 1 hour; forwarded logs are immutable in the SIEM archive; daily review of gateway, cloud, firewall and OT domain events; a monitoring plan with quarterly control metrics. Passive OT sensors cover the 9 plants on the OT standard and Terminal T1; the 7 legacy plants have none. DCS event journals (setpoint and alarm limit changes) are not a data source

title: Group: incident response plan v2025 with OT annex, SOAR playbooks and case export
source_system: Group case management system (SYS-G2); SOC document library
what_it_shows: The group incident response plan v2025 has an OT annex that puts the process in a safe state first. Its site lists do not include the 5 plants acquired in 2024, and it does not define Coast Guard or DOT reportable incidents. SOAR playbooks contain IT endpoints automatically; OT containment is manual. Incident cases are tracked in the SOC case system and correlated across IT and OT; Hazmat Transport cases are escalated with the carrier's 3-level scale. A forensic firm with OT experience and the DCS vendor's response service are on retainer

title: Group: EDR coverage report
source_system: EDR console (SYS-G2)
what_it_shows: EDR on all IT servers and workstations, cloud workloads, plant IT hosts, OT DMZ servers and the engineering hub workstations

title: Group: vulnerability, patch and advisory reports, Q1 2026
source_system: Vulnerability scanner; OT sensor findings; patch management console; OT desk advisory log; group vulnerability disclosure page
what_it_shows: Monthly authenticated scans of IT systems and cloud workloads; passive vulnerability identification from the OT sensors at standard plants and Terminal T1, with active scans of OT DMZs only; vulnerability feeds updated daily; ICS advisories triaged by the OT desk within 2 business days; patch status reported for gateway broker hosts and OT DMZ servers. The group publishes a vulnerability disclosure page and is a member of a sector information sharing organization

title: Group: cloud account inventory and IAM export, providers A and B (SYS-G3)

what_it_shows: Provider A hosts the corporate landing zone, SYS-G6, SYS-C9, SYS-D3, SYS-T1, the SYS-G4 integration services and the gateway broker hosts; provider B hosts disaster recovery replicas and the immutable backup vault. SYS-C1 to SYS-C5, SYS-C8, SYS-D1 and SYS-D2 run on premises

title: Group: landing-zone guardrail compliance report and pipeline records
source_system: Guardrail policy service; infrastructure code repository (SYS-G3)
what_it_shows: Mandatory settings (encryption, logging, no public storage) applied to every division account; unapproved service types blocked; landing-zone changes deployed through pipelines with approval

title: Group: hub firewall policy, WAN design and link inventory
source_system: Hub firewall management; network documentation (SYS-G3)
what_it_shows: Hub-and-spoke network with inspection; deny by default between spokes and to on-premises sites; division accounts reach plant OT DMZs only through approved conduits; encrypted private links from plants, branches, terminals and truck terminals to the hubs; OT DMZ servers reach vendor update sources only through the group proxy; provider DDoS protection on public endpoints with group rate limits

title: Group: key management inventory, certificate inventory and encryption report
source_system: Provider key management services; group PKI (SYS-G3)
what_it_shows: Group-managed keys per division account, with provider hardware security modules; storage and databases encrypted at rest, including the SYS-D3 managed database; gateway and OT DMZ certificates issued by the group PKI

title: Group: backup vault configuration, and job reports (provider B)
source_system: Backup service and immutable vault console
what_it_shows: Immutable vault in provider B with a separate backup identity, encrypted with group keys; vault inventory lists offline plant configuration copies. Daily backups of cloud workloads, including SYS-D3; nightly copies of the Plant C1 configuration and the division recipe library through the engineering hub; hourly backups of TMS open loads and shipping papers. All jobs in Q1 2026 completed

title: Group: central log archive and retention settings
source_system: Central log archive account (SYS-G3)
what_it_shows: Write-once log archive readable only by the SOC; retention 1 year online and 6 years archived

title: Group: training, phishing and acknowledgment records

what_it_shows: Annual security awareness for all workforce, including plant operators, with insider threat and recognize-and-report modules; completion of 98% or more at every plant (98% at Plant C1); quarterly phishing simulations; policy acknowledgments for 2025; records kept 5 years. OT security training for operators, engineers and I&E technicians since 2025, and an OT incident response training roster for Plant C1 shift superintendents and Controls Engineering in 2026. Integrator personnel who use the gateway are not enrolled

title: Group: screening, onboarding, termination, transfer, access agreement and sanctions records
source_system: Group HR system

Integrator contracts require background checks for on-site staff; no screening records for remote integrator staff were provided

Controllers and SIS components are bought from the OEM or authorized distributors. Of 6 HR, payroll and driver records SaaS contracts, 3 have no express breach notice term

source_system: Vendor portals; third-party risk management tool
what_it_shows: SOC 2 Type 2 reports on file for cloud providers A and B, the identity SaaS vendor, the LIMS vendor, the telematics and ELD vendor and the driver records vendor, with the providers' shared responsibility documentation and the identity vendor's documentation of validated cryptographic modules. No report or security review is on file for the telemetry gateway vendor

Release notification is exercised every year and technical OT playbooks were tested in 2026; no cross-division exercise of the matrix is recorded

owner: Specialty Chemicals security and compliance lead

Their Site Security Plan physical measures (fence, gate, CCTV, loading verification) are still maintained. Legacy CVI is kept in a restricted repository with an access list

title: Specialty Chemicals: Plant C1 process safety information and RMP management system document
source_system: Plant C1 process safety system
what_it_shows: Maximum intended inventories: chlorine in up to 2 connected 90-ton rail cars (360,000 lb); 50% hydrogen peroxide 34,000 gal (about 170,000 lb of hydrogen peroxide); 50% sodium hydroxide about 1,150,000 lb; 12.5% sodium hypochlorite about 2,400,000 lb. Safe upper and lower limits are enforced by DCS clamps; the SIS safety requirements specification and gas detection are documented. MOC limits keep hydrogen peroxide below 52% and flammable liquids under 10,000 lb per process location. The PSI index does not describe the control system network or remote access paths. The management system document names the Plant Manager as qualified person, with the Process Safety Manager and the Controls Engineering Manager

title: Specialty Chemicals: Plant C1 RMP submission, compliance audit and accident history
source_system: EPA RMP submission records; Plant C1 process safety system
what_it_shows: Five-year RMP update submitted 2024-06-20 (submission receipt on file); compliance audit report 2025-05-14 with all findings closed, next audit due by 2028-05-14; no RMP accidents since 2019

title: Specialty Chemicals: Plant C1 PHA 2024 worksheets and action tracker
source_system: Plant C1 process safety system
what_it_shows: PHA revalidated 2024, next due 2029; gas detection and the SIS on UPS and generator are documented. Instrument failures are treated as random; no scenario has control system compromise as a cause, and DCS alarms and some DCS interlocks are credited as layers of protection alongside the SIS. No safer technology and alternatives analysis is included. All 2024 actions are closed or scheduled

title: Specialty Chemicals: Program 2 plant hazard reviews and notification exercise records
source_system: Process safety system (4 Program 2 plants)
what_it_shows: Hazard reviews at the 4 Program 2 ammonia plants are current and do not include control system compromise as a cause; their notification exercises used office phones; cellular phones are kept in each control room

title: Specialty Chemicals: Plant C1 MOC procedure, MOC records 2025 to 2026-Q1 and recipe push log
source_system: Plant C1 MOC system; SYS-C8 recipe change and push log
what_it_shows: DCS and SIS logic changes go through the Plant C1 MOC procedure, and pre-startup safety reviews are recorded for physical changes. The MOC form has no cybersecurity screening question and OT security is not a required reviewer. Recipe changes pushed from SYS-C8 are approved at the hub and are not routed through the plant MOC screen. Logic changes are tested on the plant simulator before download, and factory and site acceptance tests include security test cases

title: Specialty Chemicals: Plant C1 procedures, safe work practices and contractor files
source_system: Plant C1 document control
what_it_shows: Operating procedures (certification record dated 2026-03-15) include emergency shutdown, loss-of-DCS and fail-safe steps; none tells operators what to do if HMI values may be manipulated. The safe work practice manual controls physical entrance and does not mention remote entry into control systems by integrators. Contractor files record safety performance evaluations for the 3 Plant C1 integrator teams and no evaluation of their cybersecurity practices. The incident investigation procedure has no question on possible cyber causes; a root cause method was selected and a procedure update is in draft. The employee participation plan was updated in 2026 with stop-work authority and an anonymous reporting line

title: Specialty Chemicals: Plant C1 training records
source_system: Learning management system; Plant C1 training files
what_it_shows: All operators are current on process safety training, and the 2026 refresher adds recognize-and-report for process anomalies; operators are trained each year on loss-of-DCS procedures

title: Specialty Chemicals: Plant C1 mechanical integrity and facility records
source_system: Plant C1 maintenance work orders (SYS-G4); SIS proof test records; facility inspection records
what_it_shows: SIS proof tests at each turnaround with checksum verification; alarm and interlock tests documented; maintenance findings tracked in work orders. UPS and standby generator for the DCS, SIS and gas detection, tested monthly, with fuel for 72 hours. Emergency lighting, fire detection and suppression, and server room leak detection inspected; control room pressurization and temperature records. Monthly chlorine detector bump tests, with detector health alarms

title: Specialty Chemicals: Plant C1 emergency response plan, coordination and exercise records
source_system: Plant C1 emergency response records; Specialty Chemicals EHS records
what_it_shows: Plant C1 is a responding stationary source with its own hazardous materials team; the plan was reviewed in 2026-04. The community notification service, cellular phones, a satellite phone and plant radios work without the business network (equipment check log current); shift superintendents carry the RQ table and the NRC number on the printed call list. Annual coordination meeting with the LEPC and county fire rescue held 2026-03-11. Field exercise with county fire rescue on 2025-10-08; its evaluation report was issued 2025-12-19. Equipment inspections and responder training are current. The OT contingency plan is part of the emergency response plan

title: Specialty Chemicals: Plant C1 production, shipping and supply report
source_system: Plant C1 production reporting (SYS-G4); supply contracts
what_it_shows: About 900 tons a day of sodium hypochlorite and blended products and about 140 outbound truckloads a day; about 60% of sodium hypochlorite goes to drinking water and wastewater utilities in the Southeast; about 30% of division volume is sold through Distribution, and about 55% of the two divisions' bulk outbound loads move on Hazmat Transport trucks. Chlorine arrives by rail from one supplier whose contract names a second origin plant

title: Specialty Chemicals: Plant C1 OT asset inventory, network diagrams and vendor support status
source_system: OT monitoring console (passive inventory); Plant C1 network documentation; DCS vendor support letter
what_it_shows: 412 OT devices with owner, criticality and firmware version, reconciled quarterly: redundant DCS controllers and server pairs, 14 operator stations, 3 engineering workstations, separate SIS controllers and an SIS engineering workstation, 46 PLCs, 38 chlorine detectors, the historian and the OT DMZ servers. Diagrams show control, supervisory and SIS networks behind the OT DMZ, with no wireless on the control or supervisory networks; security systems sit on a separate segment

title: Specialty Chemicals: Plant C1 OT account and role records
source_system: Plant C1 OT domain; DCS and SIS user administration; Plant C1 OT access procedure
what_it_shows: The Plant C1 OT access procedure implements the access section of the OT standard. OT domain accounts are created by ticket with Controls Engineering Manager approval and reconciled monthly to the HR feed (monthly reconciliation records on file); OT domain and DCS accounts are disabled within 24 hours by ticket. The SIS engineering workstation uses one shared account whose password was last changed in 2024; SIS program changes need the keyswitch and two-person verification (keyswitch log). The EWS access list is kept by Controls Engineering

source_system: Terminal T1 inventory (312 OT devices); 2022 network map; walkthrough
what_it_shows: Inventory of 312 OT devices without critical-system designation or approved-list status; the 2022 network map does not show the 2024 rack expansion. The walk-through on 2026-08-19 found USB blocked on operator stations and open ports on rack switches

title: Control assessment: Division sample (Distribution): boundary protection at Terminal T1
source_system: Terminal T1 firewall rules; passive capture on the rack segment 2026-08-19
what_it_shows: Passive capture on the rack segment on 2026-08-19: the loading rack and tank gauging PLCs share a segment with the terminal office, and sensor rules do not separate office from OT traffic

title: Control assessment: Common control (SYS-G2 SOC and OT desk): vulnerability monitoring and scanning
source_system: Vulnerability reports; OT sensor findings; KEV tracking
what_it_shows: Vulnerability reports, OT sensor findings and KEV tracking reviewed: 2 KEVs on Terminal T1 management servers were open 47 days with no documented compensating control, and 11 qualified OT patches at Plant C1 waited more than 180 days

title: Control assessment: Division sample (Distribution): external system services (telemetry vendor)
source_system: Telemetry gateway vendor contract; portal configuration; vendor review file
what_it_shows: The telemetry vendor portal signs in without MFA; the vendor file shows no monitoring or review since contract signature in 2023

title: Control assessment: Division sample (Distribution): MFA on the telemetry vendor portal
source_system: Telemetry vendor portal administrator sign-in test
what_it_shows: Vendor portal administrator accounts signed in with a password only

title: Control assessment: Division sample (Hazmat Transport): control assessments
source_system: Hazmat Transport assessment records 2024-2026; inheritance documentation
what_it_shows: Hazmat Transport assessment records 2024-2026 contain no plan listing the group controls the division inherits, and the technical measures behind the security plan (dispatch, telematics, ELD) have not been assessed

title: Control assessment: Division sample (Hazmat Transport): identification and authentication
source_system: ELD support accounts at 2 sampled terminals (2026-08-25) and fleet-wide account export
what_it_shows: ELD support accounts are shared at 6 of 28 terminals, including both terminals sampled on 2026-08-25, so support edits there cannot be tied to a person

title: Control assessment: Division sample (Hazmat Transport): planning policy and procedures
source_system: Hazmat Transport supplement v2023; group policies v2026
what_it_shows: The 2023 supplement and its procedures were not reviewed after 2023 or updated for the 2026 group policy drafts; the supplement conflicts with group policy on shared accounts, MFA, severity, termination and AI

title: Control assessment: Division sample (Hazmat Transport): risk assessment in the carrier security plan
source_system: Carrier security plan risk assessment; Vice President of Safety and Compliance interview
what_it_shows: The carrier security plan risk assessment does not identify cyber threats to dispatch, electronic shipping papers, telematics or ELDs and was not updated when electronic shipping papers were introduced in 2024
